exit_criteria: Write complete, charge-balanced arrow mechanisms of 5 steps or fewer in the course text notation for polar, radical, pericyclic and Pd-catalysed reactions
Predict SN1/SN2/E1/E2/E1cB outcomes from substrate, nucleophile or base, solvent and conformation, including Curtin–Hammett cases

Rank SN2 nucleophiles with Swain–Scott n; estimate relative rates of nucleophiles with carbocations and Michael acceptors using Mayr N/s_N/E; state where the Mayr equation is not validated (e.g., SN2 at sp3 carbon)
Distinguish concerted from stepwise alkene additions and predict their regiochemistry and stereochemistry
Draw acid- and base-catalysed carbonyl mechanisms (hydride/Grignard, acetal, imine/enamine, acyl substitution, enolate, aldol/Claisen, conjugate addition) with correct proton bookkeeping
Use FMO and Woodward–Hoffmann rules to classify cycloadditions, electrocyclic reactions and sigmatropic shifts under thermal and photochemical conditions
Count electrons and oxidation states at metal centres and trace a Suzuki cycle through its elementary steps, including competing transmetalation pathways
Design and interpret mechanistic experiments (KIE, crossover and labeling, trapping, radical clocks, Hammett ρ)
Critique ML reaction-prediction claims for dataset bias and Clever Hans effects

prerequisites: Two semesters of undergraduate organic chemistry (functional groups, nomenclature, basic reactions)
Stereochemistry (R/S, E/Z, relative configuration) and cyclohexane conformational analysis
General chemistry kinetics and thermodynamics (ΔG, ΔG‡, rate laws, equilibrium constants)
Basic MO theory (bonding/antibonding, HOMO/LUMO); polyene π MOs are refreshed in lesson 38
Oxidation states (d-electron and 18-electron counting is taught in lesson 46; prior exposure helps)
Basic NMR and IR interpretation (used in the evidence lessons)
